comments.note: getDocumentationAction omits the hasDependencyBlocked(wpDetail, rootIndex) skip guard that every other action function (getDeveloperAction, getQaAction, getReviewerAction) applies at the top of the WP loop. This is functionally safe because: (a) BLOCKED WPs are skipped at the loop header, (b) P7 explicitly guards with canStartWorkPackage, and (c) IN_PROGRESS WPs are already dependency-validated. However, the architectural inconsistency means future developers aligning Documentation against the other action functions may miss this difference. Recommend adding hasDependencyBlocked consistent with peers, or documenting the intentional deviation in a comment on the loop.

P4 REWORK guard (!hasNewUpstreamPassSince(pipelines, 'code-review', 'documentation')) was deduced from test expectations rather than specified in the WP-005 spec. The guard is semantically correct: Documentation self-reworks only when there is no fresh code-review trigger (which would route to WRITE_DOCS instead). The WP spec should be updated to document this guard explicitly so future developers understand the intent.

allCriteriaMet uses a length > 0 guard, so FINALIZE_WP never fires for zero-criteria WPs (UPDATE_CRITERIA fires instead). This matches the QA observation. The behavior is intentional and defensive. All production WPs have AC, so no immediate risk; the guard should be noted in the spec for zero-AC edge case handling.

P1b for Documentation iterates over ['implementation', 'qa', 'code-review'] in a for loop rather than using the inline OR pattern of Reviewer P1b. Both are correct; the loop is more extensible for future upstream type additions. The variation is acceptable but adds one more instance of an inline string array (same as the allPipelineTypes comment from WP-002).
